findings.reason: a node building §5 as written either wires its gate to a guard that can never fire on a stopped holder (a done-when that passes for the wrong reason) or must add the very refusal family the section promises it is not adding, so the section's stated scope and its measure must be reconciled before dispatch.
findings.text: §5 states "Promoting the holder while its descendant is live is refused through the existing live-run promotion guard, the family `--waive-live-run` already answers, naming the descendant; no refusal family is added", but that family is `_require_worker_stopped_before_promotion` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:727), which refuses only while the *promoted run's own* recorded process is alive and "not finished"; the other guard in the chain, `_require_partner_terminal_before_promotion` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:854), covers only the two arms of a paired dispatch. §5's holder is stopped by its own premise, so neither guard can fire, and nothing in promotion checks an *other* live run's ancestry against the promoted revision. The §5 done-when clause "promoting the holder while its descendant is live is refused by the live-run guard naming the descendant" therefore measures a guard that does not exist

findings.reason: the section's done-when demands that the registry and the dispatch check agree on a verdict neither can compute from the stated decision point, so the building node would discover mid-implementation that the measure, not the code, has to change, exactly the reconciliation a pre-build review exists to force.
findings.text: §5 places the new case inside `claim_disposition`, whose signature is one pointer in and one boolean out (`claim_disposition(pointer, *, integration_ref="main") -> ClaimDisposition`, reckon/crew/node.py:1500; `binding: bool`, reckon/crew/node.py:1495), yet the case it adds is relational — "a claim held by a stopped run does not bind a dispatch whose base is that run's chain tip". The dispatch's base is not an input to that function, and its two callers supply different things: `_repository_scope_claims` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:286, a global sweep of live pointers) never passes the base of the dispatch under admission, and `_live_scope_claims` (reckon/crew/runs.py:932) builds one `binding` boolean per claim row, which cannot express "not binding for the stacked run" while the section's own control requires "refuses one based on main" — the two halves of the §5 done-when are unsatisfiable at once through that one field

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1567), `claim_disposition` (reckon/crew/node.py:1500), `_live_scope_claims` (reckon/crew/runs.py:902), `_revision_is_ancestor` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:2389), `_is_ancestor` (reckon/crew/merge.py:538), `admit_until_stopped` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1316), `_record_pass_verdicts` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:922), `--waive-live-run` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2159), `crew observe` (reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2774), and `admission-verdicts.jsonl` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:59).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's done-when requires the claim registry to report the holder's claim as not binding the stacked run while the same section's own control requires a main-based dispatch to still be refused, and one boolean per claim row cannot carry both.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — landed evidence sits on durable served paths (`/reckon/evidence/archive/a-coordinator-can-clear-its-own-duties-landed.html` carries `#s2`, `#s3`, `#s4`; and `/reckon/evidence/fragments/a-coordinator-can-clear-its-own-duties/...`), with no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the symbols §5 and §6 widen carry no stage label, ticket number or version tag, and the prose states mechanisms rather than a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5 asserts the promotion of a stopped holder is refused by an existing live-run guard nobody has to add, but the guard it names fires only on the promoted run's own live worker.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2–§6 asserts one mechanism with its consequences; §5's four clauses are one admission rule and its recorded effect, not two deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan's after-pointer resolves (`plan-after: work-is-checked-against-its-domain#s2` is the section that derives the refusal from `reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py`), and followup f-accd-002's prompt invoking only §5 while titled "Build §5 and §6" follows the house chain convention already set by f-accd-001 ("Build §2 to §4", invoking §2).
